text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALE - Two Philippine mills bought 100,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat at about $185 per tonne, traders said Monday. The commodity will be shipped between May and July this year, one trader said.

TAPIOCA SALE - A South Korean feed grain buyer group, known as the Feed Buying Group, bought 49,150 tonnes of Thai tapioca at $83.89 a tonne C&F, traders said on Monday. The purchase was split into four lots: the first for 11,100 tonnes for arrival by May 10, the second for 13,600 tonnes for arrival by June 10, the third for 13,450 tonnes for arrival by July 10 and the last for 11,000 tonnes for arrival by September 10 at the western port of Inchon.

CORN TENDER - The Philippines' National Food Authority said Monday it would buy 40,000 tonnes of corn for shipment not later than April 15. The state-owned firm said in an announcement in Philippine newspapers that it planned to invite bids to supply 15,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. yellow corn on April 2. It will also seek tenders for the supply of 25,000 tonnes of white kernel corn.
VEGOIL TENDER - Egypt seeks up to 45,000 tonnes of vegetable oils for May delivery. The deadline for bids was April 2.
BARLEY TENDER - The South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.
RICE TENDER - Iran is seeking to buy 400,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand but a deal has not been concluded yet, Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said on Monday.
- Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.

MARKET TALK - Pakistan has sealed its borders to check the smuggling of wheat out of the country because of flour shortages in some areas, a government minister said on Saturday....Brazilian processor Ceva Alimentos said on Monday it was in talks to sell 150,000 tonnes of soymeal and 230,000 tonnes of soybeans to two separate firms for April 15-May 30 shipment, a company official said....Japan's third-largest convenience chain store operator said on Monday it has started selling U.S. rice at its nearly 4,500 outlets across the country....CBOT floor sources said India cancelled a tender for 500,000 tonnes of wheat.
